How Browsers Render Pages

Rendering starts when the browser parses HTML into the DOM tree and CSS into the CSSOM. The two are combined into a render tree that only contains visible nodes.

Layout

During layout the browser computes the exact position and size of each node. This step is also called reflow, and it is expensive on large documents. See MDN performance guide.

Paint and composite

Paint fills in pixels, and compositing draws layers to the screen in the correct order. GPU acceleration makes compositing fast.
